intro.title: z-index and stacking context
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple webpage with overlapping colored boxes to visually explore how z-index controls the stacking order of elements. You will learn the core concept of stacking context, which determines how elements are layered on top of each other. The main technology involved is CSS, using properties like position and z-index. By the end, you'll understand how to use z-index effectively to manage which elements appear in front or behind others.
intro.usecase: The z-index property is essential for managing overlapping UI elements in real-world interfaces. Developers use it to control stacking order in complex layouts like navigation dropdowns that must appear above page content, modal dialogs that overlay everything, or tooltips that float above form fields. In dashboards with multiple panels, cards, and data visualizations, z-index ensures interactive elements like hover states or notification badges remain visible. Understanding stacking context prevents common bugs where elements unexpectedly appear behind others despite having higher z-index values.
